newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian dollar opens flat ahead of trade data.
newsitem.headline: Canadian dollar opens flat ahead of trade data.

text.p: * Canada's dollar opened flat at C$1.3760 (US$0.7267) in light trading on Friday ahead of Canadian trade data due to be released at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT, dealers said.
* They said the Canadian dollar continued to remain soft in the absence of an anticipated move by the Bank of Canada to raise interest rates by 25 basis points.
Analysts said markets would look to the trade data for a further indication of whether the Bank of Canada might raise interest rates by another 25 basis points.
The central bank raised its key bank rate three weeks ago in an attempt to shore up a weak Canadian dollar.
"Obviously, the key thing driving the currency right now are the prospects for Bank of Canada policy," said Michael Gregory, economist and strategist with Lehman Brothers.
"A wide surplus is good for the currency, but if we get weaker exports, then that's probably negative for the Canadian dollar," Gregory said.
Gregory noted that wholesale trade numbers, also out at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT, would probably have a significant effect on the Canadian dollar.
The Reuters survey forecast a 1.0 percent increase in wholesale trade for May after a 3.0 percent jump in April.

"Wholesale trade is the only number today that provides unequivocal direction for the currency. It is a critical report because it indicates not only the level of consumer spending but also business and capital spending," Gregory.
But analysts said currency markets had already priced in another Bank of Canada rate hike.

"Now that the market has, to a large extent, priced in a Bank of Canada move, the real question is, will the Bank justify the move in the same effective manner that it did when rates were being cut?" said a trader with a Canadian bank.
On the crosses, the Canadian dollar rose against the German mark to 1.3058 marks from 1.3021 marks at Thursday's close, and jumped to 84.32 Japanese yen from Thursday's 84.08 yen.
